title: $4.5B in Bitcoin and Ethereum Options Expire as Traders Stay Cautious Ahead of Year-End Moves

Nearly $4.5 billion in Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH) options are set to expire today, December 12, 2025, at 8:00 UTC — a key event hitting markets amid thin year-end liquidity and cautious sentiment.
Traders Brace for Major Options Expiry After Fed Cut
Bitcoin is trading at $92,249, with a max pain point at $90,000. The market currently holds 18,974 call options and 20,852 puts, totaling 39,826 contracts in open interest. This puts the put-to-call ratio at 1.10, representing roughly $3.7 billion in notional value.
Deribit reports that call and put positioning is nearly balanced, reinforcing expectations of a muted expiry following several weeks of range-bound price action.
The clustering around $90,000 reflects a market waiting for the next catalyst rather than leaning into directional conviction,” the exchange wrote.
Ethereum is trading at $3,242, with a max pain level of $3,100. ETH open interest stands at 237,879 contracts, including 107,282 calls and 130,597 puts, giving a put-to-call ratio of 1.22 and about $770 million in notional value.
Deribit notes that ETH positioning has “normalized” into a more neutral spread, but heavy call interest above $3,400 suggests traders are still willing to price in potential volatility.
Macro Tailwinds Offer Support — But Caution Still Dominates

According to analysts at Greeks.live, the Federal Reserve’s 25 bps rate cut and renewed $40 billion in short-term Treasury purchases offer supportive liquidity conditions. Still, they warn against declaring the start of a new bull market.
Calling this a QE reboot or the start of a new bull market is premature,” they said, noting that year-end trading periods historically see the weakest liquidity in crypto.

More than half of overall open interest is parked in December 26 expiries, while implied volatility continues to drift lower — signaling subdued expectations for major near-term price moves.

Options markets also show a persistent negative skew, with puts trading at a premium to calls. This dynamic reflects a stable spot environment favoring covered-call strategies as well as ongoing demand for downside protection amid broader market softness.

Greeks.live warns that while structural conditions remain weak, traders should stay alert to potential upside catalysts — even if sharp moves are unlikely.
Short-Term Risks Contrast With Long-Term Strength

Deribit analysts highlight several short-term headwinds:

ETF outflows

MicroStrategy losing its trading premium

Mounting miner stress

There’s definitely risks in the near term… We’ll need one of those structural things to change,” Deribit said, citing Sean McNulty, Derivatives Trading Lead APAC at FalconX.

Still, the long-term trend for both BTC and ETH remains constructive, suggesting today’s expiry will likely remain contained unless a new catalyst emerges.
As the market absorbs the expiration of nearly $4.5 billion in options, traders appear focused on maintaining balanced exposure while watching macro liquidity shifts and crypto-specific developments heading into the new year.
In the immediate term, volatility may increase as options roll off and traders rebalance. But conditions could stabilize into next week once new positioning takes shape.
